status_summary: A narrower restriction on Chinese companies became operative in defense purchasing during the period. Under Section 805 of the FY2024 defense authorization law, enacted before the period, the Department of War's direct ban on procurement from companies on its Section 1260H list of Chinese military companies, and from entities they control, took effect on 2026-06-30, with an indirect ban on goods incorporating their products from 2027-06-30; the Department published a waiver process. A trade-press report from July 2026 says the Department issued implementation guidance and that a June 2026 list update added dozens of subsidiaries and affiliates. The restriction covers listed Chinese military companies rather than state-owned enterprises as such, and Department of War purchases rather than all federal procurement; no government-wide rule was found.

timeline.event: The Section 805 direct ban on Department of War procurement from Section 1260H-listed Chinese military companies and entities they control took effect, with a national-interest waiver process.

title: Bar Chinese state-owned enterprises from bidding on U.S. government procurement
uncertainties: Section 805 was enacted before 2025-01-20 and its 2026 effective date is a statutory schedule; the period's actions are implementation and list updates. The 2026-06-30 date comes from the Department's undated waiver page and is confirmed by the trade-press report, whose date is given as July 2026 from its URL. Public Law 119-60, the FY2026 defense authorization (approved 2025-12-18), was confirmed on GovInfo but its text was not read; a law-firm summary of China provisions names only an AI procurement restriction from it. The same summary reports that the House-passed FY2027 defense bill would refer 1260H entities for government-wide exclusion orders; this was not verified on a primary site and is not an event here. A Federal Register search for state-owned enterprise procurement rules since 2025-01-20 found no FAR or DFARS rule. How many 1260H entries are state-owned was not checked. The 2019 transit rolling stock limit is background only.
